findings.premise: The design covers every bullet of the ISSUE's fix intent: record the author, route both ways for design and code, gate on a same-party review with the existing override, rewrite the steering/guides/descriptions, and keep older work approvable.
findings.evidence: ISSUE-1716f77ba9ba017b.json body.fixIntent lists five bullets. Each maps to the design: §3.1 party fields, §3.2/§3.3 routing, §2.5/§2.6 gate with override, §3.4 written rule, and 'an unknown author or reviewer never withholds approval by itself'. The ISSUE leaves 'what the gate does with older artifacts' to this stage. One consequence the design does not spell out: the status quo it describes (attribution model 'client', as on the ISSUE's own meta, plus meta.review.model 'client' from verdicts.ts:34 / findings.ts:32) reads as controller-authored and controller-reviewed, so every unapproved artifact reviewed the old way becomes a same-party withhold needing a re-review or an override. [files: .insrc/artifacts/ISSUE-1716f77ba9ba017b.json, src/mcp/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts, src/mcp/review-step/phases/findings.ts]
findings.action: State in the Migration section that already-reviewed, unapproved controller-authored artifacts will be withheld as same-party until the daemon reviews them or the user overrides.

findings.premise: Today approval refuses only a blocking review: an unreviewed design artifact is approvable, and an unreviewed BUILD is withheld only under an enforcement setting that is off by default.
findings.evidence: gates.ts:578 throws ReviewBlockedError only when `review !== undefined && effectiveReviewVerdict(...) === 'block'`; an absent meta.review falls straight through to the approvedAt stamp. gates.ts:748-756 withholds a BUILD only when `effectiveEnforce && gate.status === 'no-review' && req.overrideReview === undefined && basename(jsonPath).startsWith('BUILD-')`. code-review/gate.ts:144-151 readEnforceFlag defaults to false. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts]

findings.premise: The controller loop of insrc_review_step stamps its review in the verdicts phase, so start.ts and verdicts.ts are the complete set of review-step files to change.
findings.evidence: For an HLD or LLD, start.ts:53-79 (`if (isDesignStage(stage))`) returns `next: 'emit_findings'`, and the review is stamped by src/mcp/review-step/phases/findings.ts:64-83 (`model: REVIEW_MODEL` = 'client', then `meta: { ...artifact.meta, review: report }`). handler.ts:60 dispatches `case 'findings': return handleFindings(step)`. verdicts.ts is reached only for non-design stages (DEF). findings.ts appears nowhere in the design, so for the two main gated kinds the controller stamp would carry no reviewedBy and the promised 'controller-loop phases refuse to stamp a review of controller-authored work' would not exist. The gate still reads 'controller' through the model-label fallback, so this is a gap rather than a wrong verdict. T4 and T12 as written would pass while exercising only verdicts.ts. [files: src/mcp/review-step/phases/start.ts, src/mcp/review-step/phases/findings.ts, src/mcp/review-step/handler.ts]
findings.action: Add src/mcp/review-step/phases/findings.ts to §3.3's call sites: stamp reviewedBy 'controller' and apply the same-party refusal there. Extend T4 and T12 to cover the findings phase for an LLD and an HLD.

findings.premise: A BUILD record has exactly two build-step writers plus one approval-time writer, and mergeWithPrior keeps an authoredBy already on the record when a later write omits it.
findings.evidence: The callers of persistBuildRecord are validate.ts:257 (build-step validate), standalone-record.ts:309 via persistStandaloneBuildRecord called from implement.ts:155 (build-step implement, Trivial route), and completion-record.ts:85 (ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion, called from gates.ts:776 and :786). standalone-record.ts:350-358 builds meta as `...prior.meta, ...rec.meta`, so a field the new write omits survives. [files: src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts, src/mcp/build-step/phases/validate.ts, src/mcp/build-step/phases/implement.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/completion-record.ts]

findings.premise: Putting the BUILD requirement in approveWorkflowTarget makes every approval of a BUILD require an other-party code review.
findings.evidence: approveArtifactByJsonPath has a second caller that never goes through approveWorkflowTarget: src/cli/services/workflow.ts:156-158, the TUI `approve(artifactPath, ...)`, which calls `approveArtifactByJsonPath(jsonPath, ...)` directly for any path. The design places the DEF/HLD/LLD checks in approveArtifactByJsonPath but the BUILD checks only in approveWorkflowTarget (§2.5 postcondition: 'for BUILD in approveWorkflowTarget'). A BUILD approved from the TUI would therefore be stamped with no code review and with a same-party one. [files: src/cli/services/workflow.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Either move the BUILD check to a helper both paths call, or route the TUI approve through approveWorkflowTarget; add src/cli/services/workflow.ts to the change sites and a test for a BUILD approved by that path.

findings.premise: An MCP stream helper built like the existing workflow-run stream helper detects an older daemon's `unknown method` answer and reports it.
findings.evidence: For a stream request with no handler, daemon/server.ts:201 sends `{ id: request.id, error: 'unknown method: ...' }`: a unary-shaped line with no `stream` field, and the socket stays open. runWorkflowStream (mcp/daemon-stream.ts:149-163) acts only on `frame.stream` values progress, delta, done and error, and its comment at :163 says 'Unknown stream kind — ignore (forward-compatible)'. A helper copied from it would drop that line and wait until the tool's timer fires, so an older daemon would be reported as a timeout, not as 'update the daemon'. The same server path (server.ts:190-199) answers a stream request for a unary-only method with a `{ id, result }` line, which the pattern also ignores. [files: src/daemon/server.ts, src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts]
findings.action: Specify that the two new helpers treat a line with a top-level `error` and no `stream` field as a terminal failure, and have T11's fake daemon send exactly the server.ts:201 shape for the `unknown method` case.

findings.premise: finalizeArtifact has one MCP caller and two daemon workflow-run callers, takes `model` and `attribution` as trailing optional arguments, and an omitted authoredBy can leave its output unchanged (invariant c2).
findings.evidence: orchestrator.ts:383-399 declares `finalizeArtifact(intent, stepOutputs, runId, elapsedMs, llmResponse, model = 'client', attribution?)`. Its callers are mcp/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts:46 and daemon/workflow-rpc.ts:260 and :283, matching 'the MCP synthesize phase' and 'both daemon workflow-run calls'. An eighth optional parameter does not disturb them. Note the argument must be threaded through each per-workflow finalizer the switch at :401-412 dispatches to. For invariant c1, gates.ts:590 records reviewOverride only inside the blocking-review branch, so the new no-review and same-party branches must record the reason themselves, as must a BUILD overridden past a missing code review, which today records nothing. [files: src/workflow/orchestrator.ts, src/mcp/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts, src/daemon/workflow-rpc.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Name the per-workflow finalizers (finalizeDefine, finalizeDesignEpic, finalizeDesignStory) as stamp sites, and state that the new withhold branches write meta.reviewOverride.

findings.premise: The gate tests for ac3 (T5, T7) would fail on today's code, and the stream helper has an injectable connect for T9 to T11's fake daemon.
findings.evidence: T5: gates.ts:576-591 approves any artifact whose meta.review is undefined, so 'a DEF, an HLD and an LLD with no review are withheld' fails today. T7: gates.ts:748-756 withholds a no-review BUILD only when effectiveEnforce is true, so the 'enforcement off' case fails today. The fixture seam exists: daemon-stream.ts:66-68 `RunWorkflowStreamDeps { connect?: () => Socket }`, with the same seam on UnaryRpcDeps at :197. Two gaps follow from the change-sites findings rather than from these tests: no listed test exercises the findings phase (ac1/ac2 for HLD and LLD), and none approves a BUILD through the TUI path. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts]
findings.action: Add the findings-phase cases to T4 and T12 and a TUI-path BUILD case to T7.

summary.prose: Every review is done by the party that did not write the work. Each artifact and build records who wrote it (the controller or the daemon), each review records who did it, and the two existing review tools send the work to the other side. Approval of a DEF, HLD, LLD or BUILD requires a review by the other party; the user can still override with a reason.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Route every review to the other party

api.name: approveWorkflowTarget

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape. A BUILD record is withheld into skipped[] when the Story has no code review, whether or not the enforcement setting is on, and when the code review was done by the party that authored the build, both known. overrideReview approves past either.

dataModelChanges.details: Optional `authoredBy` on artifact meta and BUILD record meta; optional `reviewedBy` on the design review stamp and the code-review record. Both take 'controller' or 'daemon'. Two small shared readers return the party: the explicit field when present; otherwise, for older design artifacts and reviews, the stored model label decides. For an artifact's author the label is the `model` of each entry in meta.attribution.outputs (src/workflow/types.ts:286): all 'client' reads as `controller`, none 'client' as `daemon`, a mixture or no entries as unknown. For a design review the label is meta.review.model (src/workflow/review/types.ts:142): 'client' reads as `controller`, any other label as `daemon`. An older BUILD record's author is unknown.

dataModelChanges.entity: Daemon request to review an existing design artifact
dataModelChanges.details: A new daemon stream method, workflow.review, takes an artifact path and runs reviewArtifactFile with the provider the role router resolves for the `review` role, as the TUI review service does. It refuses an artifact the daemon authored. The MCP server gets one helper to call it and one to call the existing codeReview.run, both built like the existing workflow-run stream helper.

On `start`, each tool reads the author party. Daemon-authored: today's controller loop, unchanged. Controller-authored or unknown: the tool asks the daemon to review, waits, and returns `done` with the verdict in the same turn. If the daemon is unreachable, fails, is too old to know the request, or exceeds the wait limit, the tool returns an error saying so; it never falls back to a controller review. The controller-loop phases refuse to stamp a review of controller-authored work.

The steering source, the two review tool descriptions and the daemon comments are rewritten to say: the party that did not author the work reviews it, in both directions; the review tools route this themselves; the same model on both sides is acceptable; approval requires the review. The guides and the plugin copy follow from the steering source.

errorCases.scenario: A review tool asks the daemon to review and the daemon is not running, closes the connection, fails part-way, or does not know the request because it is an older build.
errorCases.detection: The MCP stream helper sees a connection error, a close before the final frame, an error frame, or an `unknown method` answer.
errorCases.response: The tool returns an error naming the cause (and, for an older daemon, telling the user to update it). Nothing is stamped. No controller review is offered.
errorCases.userImpact: The artifact has no review, so approval is withheld. The user starts or updates the daemon and retries, or overrides at approval with a reason.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon review takes longer than the tool's wait limit.
errorCases.detection: A timer in the review tool expires before the final frame arrives.
errorCases.response: The tool aborts the request and returns a timeout error. Nothing is stamped.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as a failed review: retry or override.

errorCases.scenario: A party is asked to review its own work: the daemon is asked to review a daemon-authored artifact or build, or the controller submits verdicts or judgements for controller-authored work.
errorCases.detection: The reviewer reads the author party before stamping and compares it with its own.
errorCases.response: The request is refused with a same-party error. Nothing is stamped.
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told which party must review instead.

edgeCases.input: An artifact or review written before this change, with no party field.
edgeCases.expected: It stays readable. A design artifact's and a review's party is inferred from the stored model label; a BUILD record's author is unknown. An unknown party never withholds approval by itself.

edgeCases.input: An unapproved DEF, HLD, LLD or BUILD record that was never reviewed.
edgeCases.expected: Withheld at approval until it is reviewed or the user overrides. Already approved records are not re-examined.

edgeCases.input: An ISSUE, SPEC or PLAN with no review.
edgeCases.expected: Approved on the user's approval alone.

edgeCases.input: A daemon workflow run reviews the artifact it just authored (its opt-in finalize review).
edgeCases.expected: The review is stamped `daemon` on a `daemon`-authored artifact, so approval withholds it as a same-party review until the controller reviews it or the user overrides.

edgeCases.input: A batch approval covers reviewed and unreviewed artifacts.
edgeCases.expected: The unreviewed and same-party ones are listed in skipped[] with a reason; the rest are approved.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A review whose verdict blocks withholds approval unless overridden, and the override reason is recorded on the artifact.
Calling finalizeArtifact, persistBuildRecord or runCodeReview without the new argument produces the same output as today.
The daemon-authored path through both review tools (the controller loop) behaves as it does today.

testLevels.purpose: The Story lists no acceptance criteria, so they are defined here.
subjects: ac1: controller-authored work is reviewed by the daemon and daemon-authored work by the controller, for design artifacts and for code, through the two existing review tools
ac2: new artifacts, BUILD records and reviews record their party; older ones stay readable
ac3: approval of a DEF, HLD, LLD or BUILD requires a review by the other party, with the existing override; ISSUE, SPEC and PLAN need none
ac4: a failed daemon review is reported and never replaced by a controller review
ac5: the steering and both review tool descriptions state the rule in both directions
T1 the two readers: explicit field wins; model label 'client' reads as controller and any other label as daemon; nothing stored reads as unknown
T2 finalizeArtifact stamps the authoredBy it is given and writes the same output as before when given none
T3 a BUILD record keeps its authoredBy across a later write that omits it
T4 each review path stamps its own party: controller loop, reviewArtifactFile, and runCodeReview with each value

T6 a same-party review withholds; an other-party non-blocking review approves; an unknown author or reviewer does not withhold

T8 a batch approval lists withheld artifacts in skipped[] and approves the rest

migration.stateBefore: No record says which party authored an artifact or a build. The review tools always run the controller loop. Approval refuses only a blocking review: an unreviewed design artifact is approvable, and an unreviewed BUILD is withheld only under an enforcement setting that is off by default. The steering says review is a controller task.
migration.stateAfter: Artifacts, BUILD records and reviews record their party. The two review tools send the work to the party that did not author it. Approval of a DEF, HLD, LLD or BUILD requires a review by the other party, with the existing override. The steering states the rule in both directions.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional party fields and the two readers; stamp the author at artifact finalize and in the build-step BUILD writers; stamp the reviewer in each review path.
Add the daemon request to review an existing artifact and the two MCP stream helpers; make each reviewer refuse its own party's work.
Route inside insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step by author party.
Make the approval gate require an other-party review for DEF, HLD, LLD and BUILD, with the existing override.
Rewrite the steering source, the two tool descriptions and the daemon comments.

migration.backwardCompat: No stored data is rewritten; the new fields are optional and older records stay readable. Three behaviours change for users: (1) insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step on controller-authored work now return the daemon's verdict in one turn instead of handing the controller a review to do; (2) an unapproved DEF, HLD, LLD or BUILD with no review can no longer be approved without a review or an override reason; (3) the daemon and the MCP server must both be on the new build, otherwise the tools report a failed daemon review. Known limit: the daemon cannot run tests, so its code review reports test results as unverified.

alternativesConsidered.name: Explicit party fields, routing inside the review tools
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Record author and reviewer party as explicit fields; the two existing review tools route to the other party; the gate checks the fields.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an optional author party to artifact meta and BUILD record meta, and an optional reviewer party to the design review stamp and the code-review record. The writers that know their side stamp it. The existing insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step tools read the author and either run today's controller loop (daemon-authored) or ask the daemon to review (controller-authored or unknown). The approval gate requires a review by the other party.
pros: The answer comes from the record, not from an assumption
No new tool for the controller to learn; the steering stays simple
Uses reviewers that already exist on both sides
cons: Needs one new daemon request to review an existing design artifact
Touches two tools and the gate

alternativesConsidered.name: Infer the party from the model label
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add no fields; treat the model label 'client' as the controller and anything else as the daemon.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Derive author and reviewer party from labels already stored (the artifact's attribution and the review's model). Routing and the gate use the derived value.
cons: BUILD records carry no such label, so code authorship cannot be derived
A label is a model name, not a party; the rule would rest on a naming convention
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Covers design artifacts but cannot tell who authored a build, so code review cannot be routed or gated. Kept only as the fallback for reading older design artifacts.

alternativesConsidered.name: Steering only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Rewrite the steering to say who reviews and leave the tools and the gate unchanged.
alternativesConsidered.approach: State the rule in both directions in the steering and tool descriptions and rely on the controller to call the right reviewer. Nothing is recorded or enforced.
cons: Nothing enforces the rule; the issue exists because a written rule was not enough
The controller has no way to ask the daemon for a design review today
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Enforces nothing and leaves the controller with no way to request a daemon design review; it restates the situation the issue describes.

openQuestions: How long should a review tool wait for the daemon review? On 2026-10-04 a non-controller design review of a 40 KB design took 12 minutes for one pass and 27 minutes with its automatic second pass. A tool call may not be able to wait that long.
